content.description_p1: Data transfer rates measure how fast data moves from one location to another, typically expressed in bits per second (bps) or bytes per second (B/s). Internet Service Providers (ISPs) advertise speeds in Megabits per second (Mbps) or Gigabits per second (Gbps), while file downloads are measured in Megabytes per second (MB/s).
content.description_p2: The key difference: 1 Byte = 8 Bits. So a 100 Mbps internet connection theoretically downloads at 12.5 MB/s (100 ÷ 8). Understanding this conversion helps set realistic expectations for download speeds, streaming quality, and network performance.

content.faq_q1: Why is my download speed slower than my internet plan?
content.faq_a1: ISPs advertise in Megabits (Mbps), but downloads show Megabytes (MB/s). Divide your plan speed by 8. A 100 Mbps plan gives about 12.5 MB/s maximum download speed.
content.faq_q2: What's the difference between Mbps and MB/s?
content.faq_a2: Mbps (Megabits per second) measures internet speed. MB/s (Megabytes per second) measures download speed. 1 MB/s = 8 Mbps. ISPs use Mbps because it sounds faster!
content.faq_q3: What internet speed do I need for 4K streaming?
content.faq_a3: Netflix recommends 25 Mbps for 4K streaming, YouTube suggests 20 Mbps. For multiple 4K streams or gaming, consider 100+ Mbps connections.
content.faq_q4: How do I calculate download time?
content.faq_a4: File Size (MB) ÷ Download Speed (MB/s) = Time (seconds). Example: 1000 MB file at 10 MB/s (80 Mbps) = 100 seconds. Remember to convert Mbps to MB/s by dividing by 8!
